title: Short bands and a pianist-violinist at the Audubon job
summary: Punch says they did not cut instruments and tells of a man who played piano and violin at a job.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: In those times when they'd cut instruments out, you know, to make a short band, what would they drop out first?
Well, I don't remember us cutting nothing out.
You didn't do that at the next time? No. You see that plenty now.

Yeah, yeah, well, it was kind of, just different, different ideas. And they used to have them big bands, you know, to cut out, all them guys cut the band out, you know, like that. But I know one time we went up here in the Audubon place somewhere, on St. Charles, and we brought the same man over the river, made me another play piano. There wasn't no piano there. And I said, well, I ain't going back home, I'm going to pat. I just pat all the letters there, it was bloody red, boy. He patting the hard, that boy we lived by that a long time. Every tune we played, he just pat the whole tune out, you know.
I've often wondered why he didn't pick up some of the other instruments, he probably could have played them all.
Well, he could have played, played, played, no, that's why, one on piano. But he couldn't play no trumpet thing then. Now he decided that after I left here.
Yeah, he didn't play no trumpet thing. He didn't play nothing but piano and violin. And he didn't bring in violin that night, because there's a piano there.
